Card 3 states that "semantic exploitation is categorically different from industrial or financial exploitation because it extracts from a different anthropological layer". Card 2 is a labour-economics chapter on strike activity — the industrial case, retrieved because the query says "strike". The claim of categorical difference and the retrieval that ignores it appear in one frame.

A smaller note: card 2 arrives via SEMANTIC SCHOLAR, an aggregator whose name shares a word with the framework, in a capture about the semantic economy. Three overlapping senses of "semantic" — the framework, the aggregator, the discipline — none of them the same.

observation.transcript:
A "semantic economy strike" refers to a conceptual form of resistance within the [Semantic Economy framework](https://www.academia.edu/146238655/SEMANTIC_ECONOMY_SINGULARITY)—where digital platforms extract value from human meaning-making—highlighting the paradox that workers cannot withhold semantic labor without suppressing their own fundamental drive to mean. [[1](https://github.com/leesharks000/semantic-economy/blob/main/SPE_COLLECTED_SERIES_ZP.md), [2](https://www.academia.edu/146238655/SEMANTIC_ECONOMY_SINGULARITY)]
Core Concepts of Semantic Resistance

* The Amputation Paradox: Traditional laborers strike by withholding physical work, but semantic or cognitive workers cannot stop producing meaning without subverting their own psychological humanity. [1](https://github.com/leesharks000/semantic-economy/blob/main/SPE_COLLECTED_SERIES_ZP.md)
* The "Drive to Mean": Human language, culture, and expression are pre-instrumental and non-optional, making this layer of mental output uniquely vulnerable to systemic enclosure and extraction. [1](https://github.com/leesharks000/semantic-economy/blob/main/SPE_COLLECTED_SERIES_ZP.md)
* Semantic Exhaustion: Instead of classic industrial burnout, the limit-state of this dynamic is a civilizational and somatic depletion caused by unending platform extraction. [1](https://github.com/leesharks000/semantic-economy/blob/main/SPE_COLLECTED_SERIES_ZP.md)
* Redirection vs. Cessation: True resistance in a meaning-economy requires redirecting cultural and linguistic output rather than attempting an impossible complete withdrawal from communication. [1](https://github.com/leesharks000/semantic-economy/blob/main/SPE_COLLECTED_SERIES_ZP.md)

If you would like to explore this further, let me know if you want to focus on:

* The theoretical mechanics of semantic capital and rent
* How AI and automation change the extraction of meaning
* Real-world parallels in digital labor and platform resistance
